reviewed_by: Claude general-purpose subagent, blind judgment reviewer, round-2 fix-verification batch

samples_reviewed.question_text: There are 0 resin in one basket and 3 resin in another basket. How many resin are there in all?
Start at 0. Count up 2 more. What number do you land on?
Lara has 2 ribbons. A friend has 1 ribbon. If they put all their ribbons together, how many ribbons do they have in all?
One basket has 1 water bottles. Another basket has 2 water bottles. If you put all the water bottles together, how many water bottles are there?
Start at 0. Count up 3 more. What number do you land on?

competency_fulfillment.rationale: Word-problem framing is present ('There are 0 resin in one basket and 3 resin in another basket...'), matching 'solve problems...involving addition', but every sum shown is 2 or 3, far under the 'sums up to 20' ceiling.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Multiple contexts appear (baskets of resin, counting-on number line, ribbons, water bottles), giving genuine narrative variety rather than one repeated scenario.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: 'One basket has 1 water bottles' has a singular/plural grammar mismatch that could confuse an early Grade 1 reader; otherwise sentence length is appropriate.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Both a 'count up' number-line framing (seed 43) and 'put together' basket/ribbon framings (seeds 42,44,45) are represented, covering more than one addition model.

competency_alignment.rationale: Every sample is phrased as a real narrative scenario ending in a question, matching the word_problem/pictorial_problem concepts this node introduces.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Sums across all 5 seeds are 2 or 3; the competency's 'sums up to 20' is never meaningfully exercised in this batch, e.g. no sample sums to double digits.
